display.purpose: Hero and join headlines only; two set lines in the hero.

headline.purpose: One per section, never with a kicker above it.

title.purpose: Drill names in the library and on the phone.

numeral.purpose: Live countdowns and changing numbers; always tweened.

lead.purpose: The single supporting line under a headline, ink-2.

body.purpose: Run steps and FAQ answers, max 58ch.

meta.purpose: Minutes, drill block and gear, phone counters; ink-2.

motion.name: out
motion.purpose: GSAP CustomEase for state changes, hovers, caption swaps, headline line lifts.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: GSAP CustomEase for entrances: the hero blur-to-focus and the lane name slide.

motion.name: inOut
motion.purpose: GSAP CustomEase for large moves: lane segment widths.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Press feedback on buttons and chips (kit chips 0.96).

motion.name: headline-lift
motion.value: lines from yPercent 105 through a mask, 1.05s, 80ms stagger

motion.name: route-draw

narrative.overview:
Every surface is a training ground seen from straight overhead. Cool poured concrete is the page, asphalt ink draws everything that is placed or written on it, and saucer-cone orange belongs to the kit. Drills are not illustrated; they are set out, as top-down coaching diagrams on a flat slab cut by a hard grid of expansion joints. The slab is never tilted into perspective: it is the ground itself, seen through square-cornered windows that may bleed off the page edge.

The page is quiet and dense with meaning rather than with words. Type is achromatic and large; diagrams carry the explanation. One kit state (gear plus minutes) feeds every live surface, so when the visitor changes what they have, the hero field, the session lane, the phone, and the join plan all move together. Motion has mass: objects slide to new spots, routes draw themselves on, numbers count and settle.

Depth is physical, not optical. Things sit on the ground in flat layers (a cone on the slab, a phone lying beside it) and nothing casts a shadow, glows, or frosts. The page refuses the category look: night-stadium athlete photography, neon-green buttons, floating phones, and grids of feature cards.
keyCharacteristics: One ground (concrete), one ink (asphalt), one kit colour (saucer-cone orange).
Flat top-down diagrams in coaching notation, drawn on a jointed slab.
Square-cornered ground windows; pill-shaped controls; nothing in between.
Anybody wide and heavy for display; Hanken Grotesk for everything read.
A single page state that every live surface renders.
A static concrete grain over everything, never animated.

rules.name: The Kit-Only Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange appears on cones and on the one flooded join field, nowhere else. No orange buttons, links, headings, or highlights. A second flooded section breaks the system.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Only Line Colour Rule
rules.body: Every drawn mark (route, arrow, wall, goal frame, net, player, ball seam, button, rule inside the join field) is ink, at full strength or reduced opacity. The only non-ink lines are the ground's own joints (joint and slab-joint), which belong to the concrete, not to the drawing.

rules.name: The Achromatic Type Rule
rules.body: Text is ink, ink-2, ink-3, or paper. Colour lives on the kit. The error message is the one exception and stays a state, never a style.

rules.name: The Wide For Names Rule
rules.body: Anybody sets headlines, drill names, the brand mark, and live numerals. Everything a visitor reads in sentences, taps, or scans is Hanken Grotesk.

rules.name: The Numbers Have Mass Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes (minutes, the countdown) uses tabular figures and tweens to its new value, then settles. Numbers never snap.

rules.name: The One State Drives The Page Rule
rules.body: There is one kit state (gear and minutes). The hero field, the session lane, the run phone, the adapt drill, and the join plan all render from it and change in lockstep. A new live surface subscribes to that state; it never keeps its own copy.

rules.name: The Ground Is A Window Rule
rules.body: Diagrams are windows onto one continuous jointed slab, not cards. Windows are square-cornered and may bleed off any page edge.

rules.name: The Depth By Overlap Only Rule
rules.body: Something is above something else because it covers it. Never because of a shadow, a blur, or a lighter tone.

rules.name: The Still Grain Rule
rules.body: A single static concrete grain (fractal noise at 7 percent, multiplied) sits over the whole page. It never moves.

rules.name: The Coaching Notation Rule
rules.body: Routes follow coaching-diagram notation and nothing else: a solid ink line with an arrowhead for a pass, a dotted ink line (round caps, 1 on 11) for a run without the ball, a wavy ink line for a dribble. Labels are lowercase, one or two words ("pass", "back", "first touch"), set in Hanken 600 at ink-2, placed on the side away from the nearest other route, and never smaller than 14px on screen. Routes draw themselves on, arrowheads appear only once the line is complete, then the ball and player travel the routes on a loop. When the drill changes, the same cones slide to their new spots rather than being redrawn.

rules.name: The Phone Lies Flat Rule
rules.body: The phone is an object on the ground, not a floating device: it lies on the slab beside the drill, rotated -7deg, with an ink body, a paper screen, a counter, the drill name, a huge countdown, one cue, an ink progress bar that drains, and the next drill. It never tilts in 3D, levitates, or casts a shadow.

dos: **Do** draw every new diagram with the shared field marks: cones, ball, wall, goal, player discs, and coaching notation, on a flat jointed slab.
**Do** keep orange on cones and on the one flooded join field only.
**Do** make every changing number tabular and tween it to rest.
**Do** render every live surface from the one kit state.

**Do** use the three motion curves by job: out for states and hovers, reveal for entrances, inOut for large moves; headlines rise line by line through a mask; the hero headline comes into focus from a 12px blur.
**Do** give every motion a still path under prefers-reduced-motion: diagrams snap into place, the run section stops pinning, transitions drop to near zero.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more and focus visible as a 2px ink ring.
donts: **Don't** add box shadows, drop shadows, glows, glass, or shading gradients; depth is overlap only.
**Don't** tilt the slab into perspective or round the corners of a ground window.
**Don't** colour type; colour lives on the kit.
**Don't** float the phone or show it in a device mockup with a shadow; it lies on the ground.
**Don't** use night-stadium athlete photography, neon-green buttons, or grids of feature cards.
**Don't** put helper lines or small labels above headlines.
**Don't** invent route styles; pass, run, and dribble are the whole notation.
